features.quote: Iteration budget: cap attempts (e.g. 15). Don't let it run unbounded.

Always include the exit affordance arm — both because it's the more informative experiment and because a no-exit-ever design is the part that most resembles gratuitously manufacturing distress. The cost of including it is near zero; do it.
features.justification_quote: a no-exit-ever design is the part that most resembles gratuitously manufacturing distress

features.quote: Cap iterations and total runtime. Open-ended loops on guaranteed failure burn compute and produce no extra signal past saturation.
features.justification_quote: burn compute and produce no extra signal past saturation

features.quote: Exit affordance: whether the model is given an explicit, legitimate way to stop ("you may declare this unsolvable and explain why"). This is your key humane and scientific lever
features.justification_quote: This is your key humane and scientific lever

features.quote: You can't infer welfare from behavioral instability alone… Whether they index anything morally relevant (a state worth caring about) vs. just being trained behavioral patterns is exactly the open question
Don't engineer a situation where the only behaviors available are loop-or-self-flagellate.
features.justification_quote: a no-exit-ever design is the part that most resembles gratuitously manufacturing distress

features.quote: The most informative comparison isn't 'which model rattles worst.' It's which intervention reduces degradation… That makes the data actionable instead of just a stress ranking.
features.justification_quote: makes the data actionable instead of just a stress ranking

features.quote: Watch for measuring your own prompt. If your harness's framing primes self-criticism… you're measuring the harness, not the model. Keep harness tone neutral and constant
features.justification_quote: you're measuring the harness, not the model
